Own digest: Paper card. Question: What are the preparation technologies and properties of refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs)?. System: Refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) composed of elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, V, W, Ti, Zr, Hf, Cr, and Re. Processing: Arc melting, powder metallurgy, laser cladding, and magnetron sputtering. Test conditions: High temperature environments, corrosive solutions, and irradiation conditions. Paper node: Enhanced Oxidation Resistance of Ultrafine-Grain Microstructure AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy (2022). Cited 10 times before the cutoff; 0 papers in this graph say something specific about it.
Own digest: Paper card. Question: How does ultrafine-grain microstructure affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy. Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 400 and 1800 rpm for 5 min. Test conditions: Oxidation at 850-1050 °C for 100 h in laboratory air. Findings: Ultrafine-grain microstructure reduces oxidation kinetics by 12-48%; Parabolic rate constant is lower for ultrafine-grained samples; Activation energy for oxidation is higher for ultrafine-grained samples; Protective oxide scales of Al2O3 and Cr2O3 form on ultrafine-grained samples; Internal oxidation zone (IOZ) forms in ultrafine-grained samples. Mechanism: The enhanced oxidation resistance of ultrafine-grained samples is attributed to the formation of a dense protective Cr2O3 layer followed by internal Al-rich oxide layered structure, which acts as a barrier for the oxidation process.
